DEFINITION · qeva:1:empty-set@2

Empty set

An empty set is a set with no members; existence and uniqueness come from the declared set theory.

editorialset-theory
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

The empty set has no members. Its existence is theory-relative, and extensionality makes it unique when it exists.

EXACT

The compact statement

Empty(E) iff E is a set and ∀x ¬(x∈E). In the declared presentation, empty-set existence gives some E with Empty(E), and extensionality proves ∀E∀F[(Empty(E)∧Empty(F))→E=F].

Example

The solution set of x²=-1 over the real numbers is empty.

Boundary / caveat

Some set-theory axiom lists derive existence from separation and another existence axiom instead of naming a separate empty-set axiom.

Assumptions

  • The ambient theory proves existence of a memberless set. · Axiom of empty set @1
  • Extensionality is available to prove uniqueness. · Axiom of extensionality @1
